thread:
nina: Heads up — our onboarding sample app started pulling in 600KB of Buffer/shim code after we published the TS types change. bundle analyzer shows references to Buffer.from and tslib helpers. Edge runtime threw "global is not defined" on first page load.

sam: hmm did the types change add `/// <reference types="node" />` anywhere? that can cause editors/bundlers to think node builtins are required.

nina: yes, the new index.d.ts has `import { Readable } from 'stream'` for a helper type, even though runtime never uses stream in the browser path.

yuri: that's classic. types should never force runtime imports. move node-only types into a `types/node-only.d.ts` and keep the main declaration free of node imports. consumers with isolatedModules or tsconfig paths can pick it up when needed.

kevin: also check package.json "browser" field — if it points to the same file as main, bundlers may substitute it wrong. We should provide a browser-specific ESM build and point "module"/"browser" at it. e.g.:
```
"main": "dist/cjs/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
"browser": "dist/esm/browser.mjs"
```

sam: What about sideEffects? we never set it. Without sideEffects:false, rollup/esbuild might keep helper files that reference node. add "sideEffects": false but list any files that perform global polyfill injection as true if needed.

nina: the weird part was consumer's build still pulled in crypto polyfills even after we released an ESM build. I tracked it: a re-export file `dist/index.js` did `module.exports = require('./cjs')` when resolved by the bundler due to package exports fallback.

yuri: fix by adding conditional exports so `import` picks the ESM file. example: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

kevin: follow-up: add a tiny reproducer in `examples/edge-app` that runs esbuild with the same plugin config we recommend. put a GH action that runs build-size check and fails if > 200KB gzipped. CI should run both node and edge bundles.

sam: note for maintainers: avoid `if (!globalThis.crypto) require('some-node-crypto')` at module top-level. That will still be executed when the file is included. Use `if (!globalThis.crypto) { await import('./node-crypto') }` inside async init.

nina: I submitted a PR: - split types, - add exports field, - add sideEffects:false, - add dist/esm/browser.mjs. CI will run example build. request review from @yuri @kevin.

ci-bot: CI: example-edge-build (examples/edge-app) — size check failed (gzipped: 412KB > 200KB). See artifacts: /artifacts/1769012360.

yuri: CI shows remaining ~180KB coming from tslib helpers and a small shim for process. tslib could be tree-shaken by switching to native helper usage: set `tsconfig` to `importHelpers: true` and publish tslib as a dependency so consumers don't inline helpers.

kevin: or publish builds with transformed helpers (use esbuild/rollup with runtime helpers) and mark tslib as peer/dep depending on approach. also confirm `types` field doesn't reference node types for browser build.

sam: Also add a short line in the SDK CHANGELOG: "Breaking: types no longer include node references; if you relied on node-only types import @redwood/sdk-node-types" — quick migration path.

nina: thanks all. I'll push a follow-up with tslib as dep and tweak CI threshold temporarily while we iterate. Deploy when green. :rocket:
